Ensure you have the Repo tool installed. If not, you can install it using the following command: if you don't have it already: Create a .bin directory mkdir ~/bin Download the Repo script curl https://storage.googleapis.com/git-repo-downloads/repo > ~/bin/repo Set Permissions chmod a+x ~/bin/repo
Create a new directory where you want to store the Halcyon Project source code: mkdir halcyon Change directory to halcyon cd halcyon

Initialize the Repo tool in the newly created directory: repo init -u https://github.com/halcyonproject/manifest -b 16.2 --git-lfs info Since we've update to our versioning and source code branching system, every branch follows a clear format: Android Version.Update Number (e.g., 14.3 for QPR3). This command initializes the Repo tool with the URL of the Halcyon Project repository.

Sync the local repository with the latest changes from the remote repository: repo sync -j$(nproc --all) --force-sync This command fetches the latest changes and updates your local repository accordingly.

To foster a positive and collaborative community, we have established the following guidelines that all maintainers must adhere to. These rules define what maintainers are expected to do and refrain from doing to ensure the integrity and quality of the project. The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

The maintainers: MUST follow project technical guidelines, and maintainer requirement. MUST maintain a respectful and positive attitude within the community, refraining from engaging in arguments or insults. MUST allow core team members to inspect and review the source code they are working with. MUST NOT add or remove packages without a valid and justifiable reason. MUST NOT modify the core Halcyon source code without prior approval. MUST NOT include any modifications such as Audio Mods (e.g., Dolby, Dirac, ViperFX4Android) or third-party cameras (e.g., GCam) unless they are ported from the stock ROM of the device being maintained. MUST provide regular updates to the project, with a minimum frequency of one update per month. MUST actively participate in discussions regarding the project, especially when decisions affect the devices they maintain. MUST actively participate in project development, particularly in fixing broken code that related and miht causes ome isue/torubles on the device that being maintained. MUST thoroughly test new updates on their device(s) before submitting builds to ensure stability and functionality. MUST document any changes or additions made to the device trees, vendor files, or kernel, providing detailed commit messages to ensure transparency. MUST follow the project's standard build guidelines and not deviate from the agreed-upon setup without discussing with the core team. MUST ensure that all included features and modifications align with the project's core philosophy and objectives. SHOULD collaborate with other maintainers to share knowledge, troubleshoot issues, and help maintain the overall quality of the project. MAY propose new features, but they MUST be discussed with and approved by the core team before implementation. MUST NOT engage in any form of plagiarism or misrepresentation of work. All work must be original or properly attributed. MUST respect deadlines for major updates or releases, and notify the team promptly if they are unable to meet those deadlines. MUST ensure that all build files, device-specific configurations, and scripts are kept up to date with upstream changes. MUST NOT use official maintainer privileges for personal gain, such as advertising personal modifications as official Halcyon releases. SHOULD maintain clear communication with the team and the community about progress, roadblocks, or changes in their capacity to maintain a device. MUST promptly report any bugs or issues that cannot be resolved independently to the core team for assistance. By adhering to these guidelines, maintainers help ensure the quality and sustainability of the Halcyon project.
You can refer to the definitions of the keywords used here.

Device trees for Halcyon: MUST have proper commit authorship. MUST have clear and descriptive commit titles. MUST follow proper formatting for commit titles and descriptions. MUST include a working proprietary files list. MUST NOT ship any prebuilt APKs that do not come from Halcyon, including Google Camera and GrapheneOS Camera. MUST NOT contain any unused overlays. MUST NOT include any features that do not exist in the stock ROM. MUST NOT remove packages that are included in the ROM by default. MUST NOT include overlays unrelated to the device (e.g., QS tile order). MUST have enforcing SELinux. MAY include OEM camera ports. SHOULD follow AOSP directory and naming structure. SHOULD NOT use dirty hacks or hardcoded paths (e.g., system/etc/hosts redirection).

Kernel sources for Halcyon: MUST have a complete commit history and proper authorship. MUST NOT include any type of blocker (e.g., Boeffla Wakelock Blocker, FS blocker). MUST NOT include any type of modification (e.g., KernelSU, APatch). MUST NOT include any form of overclocking (e.g., CPU/GPU overclocking, screen overclocking). MUST be buildable with AOSP Clang. SHOULD maintain consistency with device trees, including defconfig. MUST be able to boot without modifications to init or recovery. MUST not break DTBO or recovery boot.

To become an official Halcyon device maintainer, you have to complete the following requirements: Requirement Description Android Basic knowledge of the Android build process. Linux, and Git Applicants should possess the ability to utilize Linux and Git for version control and code management tasks. Unofficial Build Maintenance Applicants must maintain at least 2 unofficial builds in 2 weeks before applying, with positive feedback from users. Authorship All code contributions must include proper attribution information to the respective author. SELinux SELinux status must be enforcing. Hardware All hardware features must be working; some exceptions may be considered. Kernel Source Devices with OEM-released kernel sources must not use prebuilt kernels. The kernel must be compiled from source to ensure transparency and proper integration. Only devices that support GKI (Generic Kernel Image) are allowed to use prebuilt kernel images. Testing Conduct thorough testing of all device fixes to ensure functionality and quality. Updates Deliver regular updates, with a minimum of two per month, to keep devices functioning optimally. Troubleshooting Ability to troubleshoot and diagnose device issues by analyzing log data.

This page provides detailed technical guidelines for all maintainers to follow when building and maintaining Halcyon. These guidelines ensure consistency and high-quality builds across all supported devices. The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

MUST use the official Halcyon build environment configuration. MUST NOT use custom compilers or toolchains unless explicitly approved by the core team. Only the default Clang provided in the Halcyon source is allowed for building. MUST ensure that the build environment is properly set up, using the correct versions of required dependencies and tools.

MUST maintain the device tree, vendor files, and kernel configuration according to upstream standards. MUST have synchronized vendor tree with defined proproetary files in the device tree. MUST ensure changes to the device configuration are properly tested before submitting builds. MUST keep all files up to date with the latest changes from the core Halcyon source. MUST NOT add unsupported or unapproved features that deviate from Halcyon’s philosophy.

Halcyon allows the inclusion of certain ported features from the stock ROM of a device, with some restrictions to ensure consistency, avoid duplication, and maintain the clean, stock-like experience of the ROM.

MUST be ported exclusively from the stock ROM of the device being maintained. Porting features from other devices that do not natively support them (e.g., Leica MIUI Camera on a device without Leica lenses) is NOT allowed. MUST function correctly on the device and be thoroughly tested for stability. MUST NOT introduce duplicate apps that already exist in Halcyon. For example, if the OEM Camera requires a gallery app (e.g., OnePlus Camera requiring OnePlus Gallery) and this creates a duplicate of an existing app in Halcyon (such as Google Photos), the inclusion of the OEM Camera and its dependencies SHOULD be restricted or rejected. SHOULD integrate smoothly with the system without conflicting with core Halcyon features or existing apps.

MUST be ported from the stock ROM of the device being maintained. MUST be thoroughly tested to ensure they work well with the device’s audio hardware. MUST NOT interfere with or degrade the performance of other system audio features.

MUST NOT include any other third-party mods that are not from the stock ROM or are not approved by the core team. MUST avoid adding features that deviate from Halcyon’s clean, stock-like user experience, unless approved by the core team. MUST prioritize the stability and performance of the system when deciding to add or remove any ported feature.

MUST ensure that all builds are reproducible by following standard Halcyon build instructions. MUST verify the stability and functionality of the build on the device before submitting it for release. MUST document any changes, including new features, bug fixes, or optimizations, in commit messages or change logs. MUST follow any specific instructions from the core team regarding upcoming changes or major updates.

All official builds for supported devices are compiled by the Halcyon build server. Maintainers are no longer responsible for building or distributing releases themselves. Maintainers are only required to maintain and push buildable, bootable source code (device tree, vendor tree, kernel, etc.) to the official Halcyon Git repositories. Keeping sources fully up to date is not mandatory, but they must remain functional for building and booting. If any issue arises, such as build failure, boot issues, or problems reported by users, the maintainer is REQUIRED to resolve it as soon as possible. This process ensures a unified and consistent release flow for all official Halcyon builds.

This method involves flashing a custom recovery first, then sideloading the ROM package. Step 1: Installing Recovery​ Enter bootloader mode by holding Power + Volume Down. Connect your device to your PC via USB. Verify that your PC detects the device using fastboot devices. Flash the boot image onto your device using fastboot flash boot boot.img. Flash the vendor boot image onto your device using fastboot flash vendor_boot vendor_boot.img. Reboot into recovery mode by typing fastboot reboot recovery in command line or navigate through bootloader and choose Reboot to recovery. Step 2: Flashing Preparation​ caution This step is required to prevent boot issues or permanent device bricking. Skipping it may leave your device stuck in EDL mode with no easy recovery. Do not skip it. Download the copy-partitions zip from here. Reboot into recovery mode. Select Apply update > Apply from ADB. Sideload the file using: adb sideload copy-partitions-20220613-signed.zip When presented with a screen that says Signature verification failed, press Yes. Step 3: Installing the ROM​ Download the latest Halcyon build. Reboot into recovery mode. Perform a Format Data. Return to the main menu. Select Apply update > Apply from ADB. Sideload the ROM using the following command: adb sideload ota-halcyon_fogos-xxxxx.zip
If you encounter any issues during or after installation, feel free to ask in our chat group for help and solutions to common problems.

Device Compatibility Required Fastboot packages can only be flashed on a limited set of devices. Not all Android devices support fastboot package flashing. Please read the device requirements section below carefully to ensure your device is compatible.

Fastboot package flashing is supported only on devices that meet ALL of the following criteria: Android Version: Launched with Android 10 or later Dynamic Partitions: Device must support Dynamic Partitions (super partition) Fastbootd: Device must have fastbootd support (userspace fastboot) These features typically became standard in devices released with Android 10+, but some older flagships may also support them.

The following device types are NOT compatible with fastboot package flashing: Samsung devices - Samsung uses Odin protocol (proprietary download mode) and does not support fastboot packages Older devices - Devices released before Android 10 without Dynamic Partitions support (even if the community has implemented a dynamic partition retrofit) Devices without fastbootd - Devices that only support bootloader-level fastboot, not userspace fastboot Some custom ROM implementations - Devices with custom bootloaders that don't implement fastbootd Samsung Devices If you own a Samsung device, do not attempt to use fastboot package flashing. Please refer to your device's specific installation method instead.

A fastboot package (often named with .zip extension) is a complete ROM package designed to be flashed through fastboot in a single operation. Unlike traditional ADB sideloading, fastboot packages: Are flashed directly to partitions via fastboot protocol Support flashing multiple partitions simultaneously Require the device to be in fastbootd/userspace fastboot mode Work with Dynamic Partition layouts Availability Fastboot packages are available since Halcyon 16.0 Bloom and later versions.

Remove Accounts and Lock Screen - CRITICAL Before flashing, you MUST remove: Your lock screen (PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint, face unlock) All accounts (Google, Samsung, Xiaomi, etc.) Failure to do so can: Lock you out of your device via Factory Reset Protection (FRP), making it unusable Permanently damage the TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) on some devices Render biometric hardware (fingerprint sensor) permanently unusable on affected devices This damage has been confirmed on multiple devices and cannot be repaired after flashing. This is not reversible. Before flashing a fastboot package, ensure you have: ADB/Fastboot tools installed on your computer USB drivers installed (if on Windows) Unlocked bootloader (device-dependent) USB cable capable of data transfer (not just charging) Removed all accounts and lock screen from your device

The method varies by device. Common combinations include: Power + Volume Down Power + Volume Up Power + Volume Down + Volume Up (press simultaneously) Consult your specific device documentation for the exact key combination.

Connect your device to your PC via USB cable and verify it's detected: fastboot devices You should see your device listed with a serial number. Check Connection If your device is not listed, check USB drivers and try a different USB port.
Before flashing, wipe the device to ensure a clean installation: fastboot -w This command will erase all data on your device.

Download the fastboot package for your device and run: fastboot update fastboot-halcyon_XXXXXX.zip Example: fastboot-halcyon_surya-16.2-20260210-1800-Alpha-GMS-signed.zip (Replace with your device's actual package filename) This command will: Extract all partitions from the package Flash them to the appropriate partitions Verify each partition after flashing Automatically reboot when complete
After flashing completes and the device reboots: fastboot reboot Or allow the automatic reboot to proceed. Your device should boot into the newly flashed ROM.

If you encounter issues not covered here: Check your device-specific documentation Ask in our Telegram group for community support Verify you followed all prerequisites correctly Provide your device codename and exact error message when asking for help Need Device-Specific Help? Welcome to the official documentation for the Halcyon Innerbloom program. This page provides a comprehensive overview of what the program is, why it exists, how it supports our development, and how you can participate.

Halcyon Innerbloom is an exclusive, community-backed support program designed for users who wish to contribute financially to the sustainability of the Halcyon Project. As a token of our deepest gratitude, donors who meet a specific contribution threshold are granted access to custom, tailored builds of Halcyon, allowing them to request specific, bespoke features that are not included in the standard public releases.

Since its inception, Halcyon has been built on a minimalist, stock-plus philosophy. Our main goal has always been—and will always be—to provide a clean, fluid, and high-quality Android experience completely free of charge. However, maintaining an independent custom ROM project comes with real-world hurdles: A Team of Students: The vast majority of our core team and device maintainers are high school and university students. We do not have corporate backing or steady engineering salaries; our personal budgets and allowances are naturally limited. High-Performance Build Servers: Compiling Android from source requires immense CPU, RAM, and storage resources. Running these server instances costs real money every month, which has historically been paid out of our own pockets. Maintenance & Personal Time: Integrating, cherry-picking, and troubleshooting custom feature requests per user requires hours of dedicated development time balanced alongside our academic responsibilities. Previously, we offered custom builds for any donation amount. While we deeply appreciate every single cent, compiling separate custom builds for very small amounts has led to severe server resource exhaustion and unsustainable financial deficits for our student-led team. To keep the project alive, protect our team's well-being, and prevent our build servers from shutting down, we have structured the Innerbloom program to balance community appreciation with infrastructure reality.

We want to address a common misunderstanding within the community: Halcyon does NOT sell features, and we do not put code behind a commercial paywall. What you are supporting: When you participate in Innerbloom, your donation goes directly toward renting the server compute power needed to compile code specifically for your request. Supporter features are exclusive: Custom features built for Innerbloom supporters are tailored specifically for them and will not be merged into the main source code. The only exception is if a requested feature is deemed broadly useful and aligns with our project's feature guidelines — in which case it may be considered for an official release, at the team's discretion. The Framing: The custom build is not a product you buy; it is a bespoke token of appreciation from us to you for keeping our servers running. Without your support, the server instance required to build your custom request literally could not exist.
To ensure fairness and sustain our server costs, we have established a clear baseline for the Innerbloom custom build program:

Detail Information Minimum Donation $8 USD / month (or equivalent in local currency) Core Benefit Access to Custom Tailored Builds with bespoke feature requests Build Frequency Limit Maximum of 2 custom build requests per 30-day period Note: Feature requests must be technically feasible and compatible with the source tree. Approved features are built exclusively for the requesting supporter and will not be included in public releases unless they meet our feature guidelines.

Compiling an Android ROM is an intensive process that takes time and server bandwidth. Limiting requests to twice a month ensures that: Every donor gets a fair turn in the build queue without facing massive delays. The server doesn't get overloaded by building daily for minor upstream commits. It encourages donors to bundle their feature requests efficiently.

Innerbloom custom build requests are scoped exclusively to Halcyon's own source code. This means we can accommodate things like custom system features, UI tweaks, behavior changes, or integrations that live within the Halcyon platform layer. The following are outside the scope of Innerbloom and will not be fulfilled: KernelSU (KSU) or any other kernel-level root solutions Custom recoveries such as TWRP or any of its forks Third-party ROM forks or modifications derived from other projects Anything that falls outside of what the Halcyon source tree owns or maintains If you are unsure whether your request falls within scope, feel free to ask @HeroBuxx on Telegram before submitting.

Every request submitted by a supporter goes through a review process by our team. We evaluate each request based on: Technical feasibility — whether it can be implemented within our source tree Team capability — whether we currently have the bandwidth and expertise to deliver it If a request passes both criteria, we will proceed with the build. If it does not — whether due to technical limitations, incompatibility, or resource constraints — we reserve the right to decline the request. In such cases, we will inform you of the reason and, where possible, suggest alternatives.

Device Eligibility Innerbloom custom builds are only available for officially supported Halcyon devices. If your device is not on the official device list, you must confirm eligibility with @HeroBuxx on Telegram first before proceeding with any donation. If you want to support the project and get your own personalized version of Halcyon: Check that your device is officially supported. If it is not, reach out to @HeroBuxx on Telegram to confirm eligibility before donating. Head over to our Donation Page and choose your preferred payment method. Ensure your monthly contribution meets or exceeds the $8 USD threshold. Submit your donation proof to @HeroBuxx on Telegram. Our build system or maintainer will process your request based on the queue. Thank you for understanding, and thank you for keeping the Halcyon Project blooming! 🌸 note The 2x build quota resets 30 days after your donation date, on a rolling basis. Unused build requests do not carry over after the reset.
